name: Kitzbüheler Altstadt
kurzbeschreibung: The historic old town of Kitzbühel delights with colorful gabled merchant homes, upscale boutiques, medieval city wall remains, and alpine flair.
beschreibung:
Overview

The picturesque historic old town of Kitzbühel in the Tyrolean lowlands is celebrated as one of the most charming and renowned alpine town centers in Austria. Nestled in a sunny valley basin between the forested slopes of the Hahnenkamm and the iconic Kitzbüheler Horn at 762 meters elevation, the historic resort town fascinates visitors through a harmonious synthesis of over 750 years of heritage, traditional Tyrolean civic architecture, and cosmopolitan flair. The heritage-listed, pedestrianized core draws travelers from around the globe with its vivid facades, wooden oriels, and vibrant market plazas. Stately townhouses, time-honored artisanal crafts, and authentic hospitality make the historic center a beloved gathering place for locals and travelers alike.

Route & Requirements

The historic town layout centers on two primary thoroughfares: Vorderstadt and Hinterstadt. The proud merchant townhouses date back in origin to the late Middle Ages, when copper and silver mining brought great wealth to Kitzbühel. Characteristic features include wide Tyrolean-style gables with deeply projecting wooden eaves, ornate facade paintings, and wrought-iron inn signs. A scenic walk takes visitors past remains of the medieval fortification walls, the historic Jochberg Gate, and the gothic St. Catherine's Church with its pointed copper spire. The eventful urban history is mirrored in lovingly restored monuments, gothic archways, and picturesque stone fountains that invite leisurely pauses and photography. Designer boutiques, master artisan shops, and traditional taverns line the cobblestone avenues. Perched gracefully on a gentle rise above town stand the parish church of St. Andrew and the Liebfrauenkirche.

Visit & Arrival

The old town of Kitzbühel is accessible 24/7 year-round free of charge. Shops and boutiques generally operate Monday through Friday from 09:30 to 18:30 and Saturdays until 17:00. Arriving by train: convenient ÖBB rail connections directly to Kitzbühel or Kitzbühel Hahnenkamm station, followed by a short two-minute stroll into the pedestrian zone. By car: via federal road B161; pay parking is available at the large Pfarrau lot or the Hahnenkamm cable car station.

Tips

The entire pedestrian core is level, paved, and barrier-free. Browse the traditional Kitzbühel weekly farmers' market on Saturdays to sample alpine farmhouse cheeses and regional specialties. Stop into a classic Tyrolean café for freshly made Krapfen pastries. In the late afternoon, golden sunlight illuminates the pastel facades of the Vorderstadt, offering ideal lighting for photography. In winter, do not miss the atmospheric Kitzbühel Christmas market featuring artisan stalls and brass bands.
